nodes.powitanie.options.[q3_start].text.t: What can be done here for the dead?

nodes.powitanie.options.[q9_grob].text.t: Where does the guard from the ruins lie?

nodes.powitanie.options.[swoi].text.t: I want to know where the ones who died on the road lie.

nodes.powitanie.text.t: Jerzy the digger stands knee-deep in a fresh grave and keeps throwing earth as you come up. "A burial, or just curious? The first I do straight off. The second you pay for."

nodes.q3_koniec.text.t: Jerzy listens to what the sister read out and nods, as if he'd heard it plenty of times before. "So an imperial messenger went astray on his way to someone who didn't want him. People die stupid, and nobody knows where to send them. Good of you to tell me. Three groats for your trouble, 'cause that's all I've got. That, and earth."

nodes.q3_po.text.t: "Quiet. Of a night the stones on the old grave glow pale, but I've learned not to look and to spit over my left shoulder. The dead have their business, I've mine. Only don't go wandering there alone after dark, if you've even as much sense as I have."

nodes.q3_start.text.t: Jerzy drives his spade into the ground and leans on it like an old crony. "I've nothing for the dead, but I've something for the living. In the coat pocket of one I buried I found a sealed letter. Imperial seal, and the man wasn't one of ours. Take it to Sister Halina at the Crossroads Shrine. She can read official writing. All I can do is dig."

nodes.q9_grob.text.t: Jerzy points his spade at the wall. "Third row from the shrine, right by the wall. I dug his grave with my own hands, though nobody asked, because he was a decent sort. I put a stone on it. Anyone who asks, I always tell. Hardly anyone asks."

nodes.swoi.text.t: Jerzy pulls off his cap, and for him that's as good as putting on mourning. "On the road? The tribute party from the school? They were buried where they fell, no priest and no cross. If you like, I'll put up a cross for them here. Free. The dead don't pay, but I remember."
